summary: Feed s153_double to IDS is degraded: 51.8% of TCP sessions are one-way and 16.9% of frames are sliced to 256 bytes. IDS requires both directions and full payload for TCP reassembly and signature matching.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / TAP aggregation is not delivering both directions of the same session to this IDS port. 103 of 199 TCP sessions (51.8%) show only one direction, typical of SPAN configured for RX-only, missing aggregation group, or per-flow load-balancing that hashes client->server and server->client to different tool ports (asymmetric routing not aggregated).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP state tracking and stream reassembly. With only one side, handshakes never complete, state tables time out, and bidirectional signatures (request/response, C2, exfiltration) fail to fire, causing major detection gaps.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port on the packet broker so TCP reassembly sees client and server sides together.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/truncation is enabled and cutting frames to ~256 bytes. 391 of 2319 frames (16.9%) are cut short, consistent with a broker slice policy to save bandwidth/tool load.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true. Truncation removes L7 payload beyond 256 bytes, so HTTP bodies, TLS handshakes, file transfers and IDS signatures that match on payload content cannot be evaluated, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing for this IDS feed so the tool receives full packets up to 1518 bytes for complete payload inspection; use filtering or dedicated load-balancing instead of slicing to manage load.
